rows.question: What is the current building key, building street address, city, state, and postal code of the history department?
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  fba.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  TRIM(
    CONCAT(
      NULLIF(fba.STREET_NUMBER, ''),
      COALESCE(fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX, ''),
      CASE WHEN fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL) ELSE '' END,
      CASE WHEN fba.STREET_NAME IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NAME <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.STREET_NAME) ELSE '' END,
      CASE WHEN fba.STREET_SUFFIX IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_SUFFIX <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.STREET_SUFFIX) ELSE '' END,
      CASE WHEN fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL) ELSE '' END
    )
  ) AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  fba.CITY AS CITY,
  fba.STATE AS STATE,
  fba.POSTAL_CODE AS POSTAL_CODE
FROM fac_building_address fba
-- fac_building_address.BUILDING_KEY links to fac_building.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
JOIN fac_building fb
  ON fba.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
-- DLC_NAME exists on tables like fclt_organization, fclt_organization_hist, master_dept_hierarchy, hr_org_unit, etc.
-- Try to find DLC_NAME = 'History' (case-insensitive) from the most direct tables that carry DLC_NAME.
LEFT JOIN fclt_organization fo
  ON fo.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN fclt_organization_hist foh
  ON foh.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN hr_org_unit hu
  ON hu.DLC_KEY = COALESCE(fo.DLC_KEY, foh.DLC_KEY)
LEFT JOIN master_dept_hierarchy mdh
  ON mdh.DLC_KEY = COALESCE(fo.DLC_KEY, foh.DLC_KEY, hu.DLC_KEY)
WHERE fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET'
  AND LOWER(COALESCE(fo.DLC_NAME, foh.DLC_NAME, hu.DLC_NAME, mdh.DLC_NAME, '')) = LOWER('History')
ORDER BY BUILDING_KEY

rows.question: Show the unique activity titles, locations, term start date, and supervisor name for all independent activities, sorted by the ascending order of start date.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH independent_sections AS (
  -- identify sections marked as independent activities
  SELECT
    so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS subject_offering_id,
    so.SUBJECT_TITLE                AS activity_title,
    so.MEET_PLACE                   AS meet_place,
    so.TERM_CODE                    AS term_start_date,
    so.SECTION_ID                   AS section_id,
    -- canonical flags that may indicate an independent activity
    so.CLUSTER_TYPE,
    so.FORM_TYPE,
    so.IS_MASTER_SECTION,
    so.IS_LECTURE_SECTION,
    so.IS_LAB_SECTION
  FROM subject_offered so
  WHERE
    so.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL
    AND (
      so.CLUSTER_TYPE = 'Independent Activity'
      OR so.FORM_TYPE = 'Independent Activity'
      -- fallback heuristic: not a lecture or lab and marked master (common for independent activity sections)
      OR (so.IS_MASTER_SECTION = 'Y' AND (so.IS_LECTURE_SECTION IS NULL OR so.IS_LECTURE_SECTION = 'N') AND (so.IS_LAB_SECTION IS NULL OR so.IS_LAB_SECTION = 'N'))
    )
),
library_instructors AS (
  -- library table contains instructor names and a unit/role-like column; treat INSTRUCTOR_NAME as the person identifier
  SELECT
    lci.COURSE_NAME,
    lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME,
    lci.DATE_FROM,
    lci.DATE_TO,
    lci.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
  FROM library_course_instructor lci
),
persons AS (
  -- canonical person lookup; keep MIT_ID and FULL_NAME for matching
  SELECT
    MIT_ID,
    FULL_NAME,
    KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE
  FROM opa_person_current
)
SELECT DISTINCT
  i.activity_title AS ACTIVITY_TITLE,
  i.meet_place     AS MEET_PLACE,
  i.term_start_date AS TERM_START_DATE,
  p.FULL_NAME      AS SUPERVISOR_NAME
FROM independent_sections i
-- match library instructor rows to the activity by course/subject title (best-effort)
LEFT JOIN library_instructors l
  ON l.COURSE_NAME = i.activity_title
  -- restrict library instructor date range to include the term code when possible
  AND (l.DATE_FROM IS NULL OR l.DATE_FROM <= i.term_start_date)
  AND (l.DATE_TO   IS NULL OR l.DATE_TO   >= i.term_start_date)
-- join to person table; match by name (FULL_NAME or KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE) depending on available data
LEFT JOIN persons p
  ON p.FULL_NAME = l.INSTRUCTOR_NAME OR p.KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE = l.INSTRUCTOR_NAME
-- only include supervisors identified as "Activity leader" in library records.
-- The schema does not have an explicit PERSON_ROLE column in library_course_instructor, so check common place COURSE_NAME or UNIT for role text.
-- Try to filter rows where the library tables explicitly mention 'Activity leader' in either COURSE_NAME or UNIT (best-effort).
WHERE
  (
    (l.INSTRUCTOR_NAME IS NOT NULL AND (
        l.COURSE_NAME = 'Activity leader'
        OR l.COURSE_NAME LIKE '%Activity leader%'
        OR l.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE LIKE '%Activity leader%' -- unlikely but harmless
    ))
    -- if library doesn't encode role, attempt to infer by matching person title 'Activity leader' in opa_person_current.FULL_NAME is not feasible,
    -- so allow rows where COURSE_NAME matches the activity and the person exists (this preserves matches when role column absent).
    OR (
      l.INSTRUCTOR_NAME IS NOT NULL
      AND (l.COURSE_NAME = i.activity_title OR l.COURSE_NAME LIKE CONCAT('%', i.activity_title, '%'))
      AND (
        -- attempt another heuristic: if COURSE_NAME contains 'Activity' this likely indicates activity leadership
        l.COURSE_NAME LIKE '%Activity%'
        OR l.COURSE_NAME LIKE '%Leader%'
      )
    )
  )
ORDER BY TERM_START_DATE ASC

rows.question: List the unique course instructor names, course titles, and the amount of material for each course instructor key and the key of subject offered.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  DISTINCT lrci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS instructor_name,
  lrci.COURSE_NAME AS course_title,
  COUNT(lrmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY) AS material_amount,
  lrci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY AS course_instructor_key,
  lrs.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AS subject_key
FROM library_course_instructor lrci
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail lrmd
  ON lrci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY = lrmd.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY
LEFT JOIN library_subject_offered lrs
  ON lrmd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = lrs.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
GROUP BY
  lrci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY,
  lrs.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
  lrci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME,
  lrci.COURSE_NAME

rows.question: What is the room, floor, building key, building street address, city, state, and postal code of Professor Summer Haynes's office?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH employee_to_building_join AS (
SELECT
  ed.MIT_ID                                   AS PERSON_ID,
  ed.FULL_NAME                                AS FULL_NAME,
  ed.OFFICE_LOCATION                          AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  NULL                                        AS ROOM,
  NULL                                        AS FLOOR,
  ed.OFFICE_LOCATION                          AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS                   AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  -- buildings table does not have CITY/STATE/POSTAL_CODE columns in this schema;
  -- postal/city/state exist on fac_building_address / fclt_building_address tables.
  -- To satisfy the required output columns coming from buildings, we attempt to pull them from buildings.
  -- If not present, they will be NULL here (per instruction not to substitute stored values from other tables).
  bld_addr.CITY                               AS CITY,
  bld_addr.STATE                              AS STATE,
  bld_addr.POSTAL_CODE                        AS POSTAL_CODE
FROM employee_directory AS ed
LEFT JOIN buildings AS b
  ON ed.OFFICE_LOCATION = b.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN fac_building_address AS bld_addr
  ON b.BUILDING_KEY = bld_addr.BUILDING_KEY
)
SELECT
  `ROOM` AS room,
  `FLOOR` AS floor,
  `BUILDING_KEY` AS building_key,
  `BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS` AS building_street_address,
  `CITY` AS city,
  `STATE` AS state,
  `POSTAL_CODE` AS postal_code
FROM employee_to_building_join
WHERE `FULL_NAME` = 'Haynes, Summer'
  AND `ADDRESS_PURPOSE` = 'STREET'
LIMIT 1

rows.question: List the unique full room names, their corresponding building names, street addresses, cities, states, postal codes, and building heights for rooms associated with subjects that Computer Science students can enroll in.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  r.FULL_ROOM_NAME AS FULL_ROOM_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  fba.STREET_NAME AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  fba.CITY AS CITY,
  fba.STATE AS STATE,
  fba.POSTAL_CODE AS POSTAL_CODE,
  fb.BUILDING_HEIGHT AS BUILDING_HEIGHT
FROM (
  -- derive a stable full room name and building key from fac_rooms
  SELECT
    fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY AS FAC_ROOM_KEY,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(fr.ROOM_FULL_NAME, ''), CONCAT_WS(' ', fr.FLOOR, fr.ROOM)) AS FULL_ROOM_NAME,
    fr.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
    fr.ROOM AS ROOM,
    fr.SPACE_ID AS SPACE_ID
  FROM fac_rooms fr
) r
JOIN fac_rooms fr_match ON fr_match.FAC_ROOM_KEY = r.FAC_ROOM_KEY
-- join subjects offered for Electrical Eng & Computer Sci where the meeting place references this room
JOIN subject_offered so
  ON (
       (so.MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL AND so.MEET_PLACE <> '' AND so.MEET_PLACE = r.FULL_ROOM_NAME)
    OR (so.MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL AND so.MEET_PLACE <> '' AND so.MEET_PLACE = fr_match.ROOM)
    OR (so.MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL AND so.MEET_PLACE <> '' AND so.MEET_PLACE = fr_match.SPACE_ID)
     )
  AND so.OFFER_DEPT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'
-- ensure there is a matching building record (per requirement)
JOIN buildings b ON b.BUILDING_KEY = r.BUILDING_KEY
-- building height comes from fac_building (FAC_BUILDING_KEY matches buildings.BUILDING_KEY)
LEFT JOIN fac_building fb ON fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
-- only include street addresses
LEFT JOIN fac_building_address fba
  ON fba.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
  AND fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET'

rows.question: List the unique term code, subject title, room, floor, building key, building street address, city, state, and postal code, formats, and number of enrolled students for all courses with more than 300 attendees.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH parsed_room_building_identifiers AS (
SELECT
  cso.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID,
  cso.`MEET_PLACE` AS MEET_PLACE,
  NULL AS ROOM,
  cso.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID_dup,
  cso.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
  cso.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  NULL AS ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
  NULL AS FORMAT,
  cso.`TERM_DURATION` AS TERM_DURATION,
  -- parsed building number/code extracted from MEET_PLACE using common patterns:
  -- try "BldgName Room", "BUILDING_NUMBER-ROOM", "BUILDING_NUMBER ROOM", "BUILDING_NUMBER/ROOM", or leading token that looks like building number
  TRIM(
    NULLIF(
      NULLIF(
        -- pattern: token before first space if it matches letters+digits or digits
        REGEXP_SUBSTR(cso.`MEET_PLACE`, '^[A-Za-z0-9#\-]+'),
        ''
      ),
      ''
    )
  ) AS parsed_building_code,
  -- normalized room: everything after a separator like space, dash, slash, or comma, or the trailing token that looks like room number
  TRIM(
    CASE
      WHEN cso.`MEET_PLACE` IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN cso.`MEET_PLACE` REGEXP '^[A-Za-z0-9#\\-]+[\\s\\-/,]+(.+)$' THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(cso.`MEET_PLACE`, '^[A-Za-z0-9#\\-]+[\\s\\-/,]+(.+)$', '\\1')
      WHEN cso.`MEET_PLACE` REGEXP '[\\s\\-/,]+[A-Za-z0-9#\\-]+$' THEN REGEXP_SUBSTR(cso.`MEET_PLACE`, '[A-Za-z0-9#\\-]+$')
      ELSE cso.`MEET_PLACE`
    END
  ) AS normalized_room
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cso
),
building_addresses_street AS (
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  addr.ADDRESS_PURPOSE AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  addr.CITY AS CITY,
  addr.STATE AS STATE,
  addr.POSTAL_CODE AS POSTAL_CODE
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN fac_building_address addr
  ON addr.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
WHERE addr.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET'
),
room_floor_and_building_key AS (
SELECT
  -- fac_rooms columns (carry through as-is)
  `fac_rooms`.`FAC_ROOM_KEY`                                                  AS `ROOM_ID`,
  `fac_rooms`.`ROOM`                                                          AS `ROOM_NUMBER`,
  `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY`                                                  AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  `fac_rooms`.`FLOOR`                                                         AS `FLOOR`,

  -- fclt_rooms columns (carry through as-is)
  `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_ROOM_KEY`                                                AS `FCLT_ROOM_ID`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`ROOM`                                                         AS `FCLT_ROOM_NUMBER`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`                                            AS `FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`FLOOR`                                                        AS `FCLT_FLOOR`,

  -- space_unit2.room identifiers (carry through as-is)
  `space_unit2`.`SPACE_UNIT_KEY`                                              AS `space_unit2_room_id`,

  -- space_floor.floor (carry through as-is)
  `space_floor`.`FLOOR`                                                       AS `space_floor_floor`,

  -- space_detail.room id (carry through as-is)
  `space_detail`.`BUILDING_ROOM`                                              AS `space_detail_room_id`
FROM `fac_rooms`
LEFT JOIN `fclt_rooms`
  ON `fac_rooms`.`FAC_ROOM_KEY` = `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_ROOM_KEY`
  -- also attempt join by room/building pair if the PK keys don't match
  OR (
       `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY` = `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`
       AND `fac_rooms`.`ROOM` = `fclt_rooms`.`ROOM`
     )
LEFT JOIN `space_detail`
  ON `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY` = `space_detail`.`BUILDING_KEY`
  AND `fac_rooms`.`FLOOR_KEY` = `space_detail`.`FLOOR_KEY`
  AND `fac_rooms`.`ROOM` = `space_detail`.`BUILDING_ROOM`
LEFT JOIN `space_unit2`
  ON `space_detail`.`SPACE_UNIT_KEY` = `space_unit2`.`SPACE_UNIT_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `space_floor`
  ON `fac_rooms`.`FLOOR_KEY` = `space_floor`.`FLOOR_KEY`
)
SELECT
  parsed_room_building_identifiers.TERM_CODE AS term_code,
  parsed_room_building_identifiers.SUBJECT_TITLE AS subject_title,
  parsed_room_building_identifiers.normalized_room AS room,
  room_floor_and_building_key.FLOOR AS floor,
  room_floor_and_building_key.BUILDING_KEY AS building_key,
  building_addresses_street.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS AS building_street_address,
  building_addresses_street.CITY AS city,
  building_addresses_street.STATE AS state,
  building_addresses_street.POSTAL_CODE AS postal_code,
  parsed_room_building_identifiers.FORMAT AS formats,
  parsed_room_building_identifiers.ENROLLED_STUDENTS AS enrolled_students
FROM parsed_room_building_identifiers
LEFT JOIN room_floor_and_building_key
  ON parsed_room_building_identifiers.normalized_room = room_floor_and_building_key.ROOM_NUMBER
     AND parsed_room_building_identifiers.parsed_building_code = room_floor_and_building_key.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN building_addresses_street
  ON room_floor_and_building_key.BUILDING_KEY = building_addresses_street.BUILDING_KEY
     AND building_addresses_street.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET'
WHERE parsed_room_building_identifiers.ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 300
ORDER BY parsed_room_building_identifiers.ENROLLED_STUDENTS DESC

rows.question: What are the subject titles, their material titles, ISBN numbers, and total costs of new materials for each subject title?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH subject_base AS (
  SELECT
    so.SUBJECT_ID AS subject,
    so.SUBJECT_TITLE AS subject_title
  FROM subject_offered AS so
),
material_base AS (
  SELECT
    lrm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS catalog_key,
    lrc.CATALOG_TITLE AS material_title,
    lrc.CATALOG_ISBN AS isbn,
    tm.NEW_SHELF_PRICE AS cost,
    -- consider material "new" when NEW_SHELF_PRICE IS NOT NULL (per instructions)
    CASE WHEN tm.NEW_SHELF_PRICE IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_new,
    -- carry keys to remain joinable
    lrm.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
    lrm.TERM_CODE,
    lrm.SUBJECT_ID AS subject_id
  FROM library_reserve_matrl_detail lrm
  LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog lrc
    ON lrm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
  LEFT JOIN tip_material tm
    ON tm.ISBN IS NOT NULL
       AND lrc.CATALOG_ISBN IS NOT NULL
       AND tm.ISBN = lrc.CATALOG_ISBN
),
subject_material_link AS (
  -- link subjects (by SUBJECT_ID) to catalog items (catalog_key) via the detail table
  SELECT
    lrm.SUBJECT_ID                                 AS subject_offered_id,
    lrm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY                AS catalog_key
  FROM library_reserve_matrl_detail lrm
)
SELECT
  sb.subject_title AS subject_title,
  mb.material_title AS material_title,
  mb.isbn AS isbn,
  st.total_new_material_cost
FROM subject_base sb
JOIN subject_material_link sml
  ON sb.subject = sml.subject_offered_id
JOIN material_base mb
  ON sml.catalog_key = mb.catalog_key
JOIN (
  -- compute total new-material cost per subject (sum of NEW_SHELF_PRICE where considered new)
  SELECT
    subject_offered_id,
    SUM(COALESCE(mb2.cost,0)) AS total_new_material_cost
  FROM subject_material_link sml2
  JOIN material_base mb2
    ON sml2.catalog_key = mb2.catalog_key
  WHERE mb2.is_new = 1
  GROUP BY subject_offered_id
) st
  ON sb.subject = st.subject_offered_id
WHERE mb.is_new = 1
ORDER BY sb.subject_title ASC, mb.material_title ASC

rows.question: List the long names of buildings constructed before 1950 that have more than 100 employees, the built year of the building, and number of employees.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH building_basic_info AS (
  SELECT
    b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_ID,
    b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
    b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
    COALESCE(fb.DATE_BUILT, fclt.DATE_BUILT, fclt_hist.DATE_BUILT) AS DATE_BUILT_RAW
  FROM buildings b
  LEFT JOIN fac_building fb
    ON fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
  LEFT JOIN fclt_building fclt
    ON fclt.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
  LEFT JOIN fclt_building_hist fclt_hist
    ON fclt_hist.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
),
building_parsed AS (
  SELECT
    BUILDING_ID,
    BUILDING_NUMBER,
    BUILDING_NAME,
    DATE_BUILT_RAW,
    -- parse DATE_BUILT_RAW using known format '%m/%d/%Y'; produce NULL for unparseable values
    CASE
      WHEN DATE_BUILT_RAW IS NULL OR DATE_BUILT_RAW = '' THEN NULL
      WHEN STR_TO_DATE(DATE_BUILT_RAW, '%m/%d/%Y') IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE CAST(DATE_FORMAT(STR_TO_DATE(DATE_BUILT_RAW, '%m/%d/%Y'), '%Y') AS SIGNED)
    END AS built_year
  FROM building_basic_info
),
emp_counts AS (
  /* Count employees by OFFICE_LOCATION (as present in employee_directory).
     We'll also count by matching OFFICE_LOCATION to BUILDING_NUMBER or BUILDING_KEY where OFFICE_LOCATION equals those values.
     To be safe, derive counts by OFFICE_LOCATION and separately attempt to map those locations to buildings via BUILDING_NUMBER or BUILDING_KEY. */
  SELECT
    ed.OFFICE_LOCATION AS OFFICE_LOCATION,
    COUNT(*) AS employees
  FROM employee_directory ed
  WHERE ed.OFFICE_LOCATION IS NOT NULL AND ed.OFFICE_LOCATION <> ''
  GROUP BY ed.OFFICE_LOCATION
),
building_employee_map AS (
  -- map employee counts to buildings by matching OFFICE_LOCATION to BUILDING_NUMBER or BUILDING_KEY
  SELECT
    bp.BUILDING_ID,
    bp.BUILDING_NUMBER,
    bp.BUILDING_NAME,
    bp.built_year,
    COALESCE(ec.employees, 0) AS employees
  FROM building_parsed bp
  LEFT JOIN emp_counts ec
    ON ec.OFFICE_LOCATION = bp.BUILDING_NUMBER
  -- if no match by BUILDING_NUMBER, attempt match by BUILDING_ID (BUILDING_KEY)
  LEFT JOIN emp_counts ec2
    ON ec2.OFFICE_LOCATION = bp.BUILDING_ID
  -- prefer ec.employees (match by number), else use ec2.employees (match by key)
  -- Note: use a derived selection to choose preference
),
building_employee_final AS (
  SELECT
    bem.BUILDING_ID,
    bem.BUILDING_NUMBER,
    bem.BUILDING_NAME,
    bem.built_year,
    -- pick non-zero/non-null employees from the first join if present, else from second join via COALESCE
    -- Because the previous CTE used two LEFT JOINs but didn't expose ec2, re-create mapping deterministically:
    COALESCE(
      (SELECT employees FROM emp_counts e1 WHERE e1.OFFICE_LOCATION = bem.BUILDING_NUMBER LIMIT 1),
      (SELECT employees FROM emp_counts e2 WHERE e2.OFFICE_LOCATION = bem.BUILDING_ID LIMIT 1),
      0
    ) AS employees
  FROM building_parsed bem
)
SELECT
  bef.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  bef.built_year AS built_year,
  bef.employees AS number_of_employees
FROM building_employee_final bef
WHERE bef.built_year IS NOT NULL
  AND bef.built_year < 1950
  AND bef.employees > 100
ORDER BY bef.built_year ASC

rows.question: For each building key, what is the building name and the number of courses offered by the Center for International Studies?
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS building_key,
  NULLIF(TRIM(b.BUILDING_NAME), '') AS building_name,
  COALESCE(cc.course_count, 0) AS course_count
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    mb.BUILDING_KEY,
    COUNT(DISTINCT
      CASE
        WHEN c.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND c.SUBJECT_ID <> '' THEN CONCAT(c.SUBJECT_ID, '||', COALESCE(c.SUBJECT_NUMBER, ''))
        ELSE CONCAT('MASTER::', COALESCE(c.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, ''))
      END
    ) AS course_count
  FROM cis_course_catalog c
  -- The schema does not include a direct MEET_PLACE in cis_course_catalog.
  -- The user-mentioned failure was due to referencing c.MEET_PLACE. The closest
  -- place-to-building mapping available in the provided schema is joining
  -- cis_course_catalog to buildings by matching cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_CODE or
  -- SUBJECT_ID to nothing meaningful for buildings; however the original intent
  -- seems to have been to match a room/building identifier. The only sensible
  -- available join in the given schema is to attempt matching cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_CODE
  -- or SUBJECT_ID to buildings.BUILDING_NUMBER only if those fields contain building numbers.
  -- Here we attempt a best-effort join using SUBJECT_CODE = BUILDING_NUMBER and also
  -- SUBJECT_ID = BUILDING_NUMBER (using UNION of possibilities) so any course rows
  -- that list a building-like code will be counted for that building.
  JOIN buildings mb
    ON mb.BUILDING_NUMBER = c.SUBJECT_CODE
    OR mb.BUILDING_NUMBER = c.SUBJECT_ID
  WHERE (c.SUBJECT_ID LIKE '%CIS%' OR c.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID LIKE '%CIS%' OR c.DEPARTMENT_CODE LIKE '%CIS%' OR c.DEPARTMENT_NAME LIKE '%Center for International Studies%' OR c.DEPARTMENT_NAME LIKE '%CIS%')
  GROUP BY mb.BUILDING_KEY
) cc ON cc.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
ORDER BY b.BUILDING_KEY

rows.question: What is the name of the building that accomodates the most students, and how many students does it accomodate?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH buildings_chosen_capacity AS (
  SELECT
    b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_CODE,
    b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
    b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS BUILDING_COUNTER,
    b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
    b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
    /* choose capacity column per priority: BUILDING_COUNTER, then BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, then BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE.
       Only accept non-NULL integer (or integral numeric) non-negative values. */
    CASE
      WHEN b.BUILDING_COUNTER IS NOT NULL THEN 'BUILDING_COUNTER'
      WHEN b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NOT NULL THEN 'BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE'
      WHEN b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NOT NULL THEN 'BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS CHOSEN_CAPACITY_COLUMN,
    CASE
      WHEN b.BUILDING_COUNTER IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS SIGNED)
      WHEN b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NOT NULL
           AND TRUNCATE(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,0) = b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
      THEN CAST(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS SIGNED)
      WHEN b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NOT NULL
           AND TRUNCATE(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,0) = b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
      THEN CAST(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS SIGNED)
      ELSE NULL
    END AS CHOSEN_CAPACITY_VALUE
  FROM buildings b
),
max_capacity AS (
  SELECT MAX(CHOSEN_CAPACITY_VALUE) AS max_value
  FROM buildings_chosen_capacity
  WHERE CHOSEN_CAPACITY_VALUE IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  c.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  c.CHOSEN_CAPACITY_VALUE AS CAPACITY_VALUE,
  c.CHOSEN_CAPACITY_COLUMN AS CAPACITY_COLUMN
FROM buildings_chosen_capacity c
JOIN max_capacity m ON c.CHOSEN_CAPACITY_VALUE = m.max_value
WHERE c.CHOSEN_CAPACITY_VALUE IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY c.CHOSEN_CAPACITY_VALUE DESC, c.BUILDING_NAME

rows.question: List the name and floor of the building with the largest floor number.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH buildings_with_numeric_floor AS (
  SELECT
    `BUILDING_KEY` AS `building_id`,
    `BUILDING_NAME` AS `building_name`,
    `BUILDING_COUNTER` AS `building_counter`,
    CAST(`BUILDING_COUNTER` AS SIGNED) AS `building_counter_num`
  FROM `buildings`
  WHERE `BUILDING_COUNTER` IS NOT NULL
    AND TRIM(`BUILDING_COUNTER`) <> ''
    AND TRIM(`BUILDING_COUNTER`) REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$'
),
max_building_floor_value AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(`building_counter_num`) AS `building_counter_num`
  FROM buildings_with_numeric_floor
)
SELECT
  bwnf.building_name AS BUILDING_NAME,
  bwnf.building_counter AS BUILDING_COUNTER
FROM buildings_with_numeric_floor bwnf
JOIN max_building_floor_value mbfv
  ON bwnf.building_counter_num = mbfv.building_counter_num
ORDER BY bwnf.building_counter_num DESC

rows.question: For each IAP category and academic year, list the category name, academic year, total fee collected, total number of IAP subjects, and the minimum and maximum enrollment.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH iap_cleaned_numeric_fields AS (
  SELECT
    so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID,
    -- use the course catalog / subject_offered term code as academic year field per schema naming
    so.TERM_CODE AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
    cat.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME AS CATEGORY_TITLE,
    -- enrollment: prefer SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER from subject_offered / summary (already int)
    CAST(so.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER AS SIGNED) AS ENROLLMENT,
    -- fee from iap_subject_detail (already int)
    CAST(iap.FEE AS SIGNED) AS FEE_CHARGED
  FROM subject_offered AS so
  -- join iap_subject_detail: link by TERM_CODE and SUBJECT keys. iap_subject_detail stores IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY etc.
  -- The schema does not provide a direct SUBJECT_ID in iap_subject_detail; many implementations link subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID
  -- to iap_subject_detail via SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY / SESSION key is ambiguous. We'll join by TERM_CODE and SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY = IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY where possible,
  -- but to be safe include also a join on TERM_CODE only and require the iap detail to indicate it's an IAP activity.
  LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail AS iap
    ON so.TERM_CODE = iap.TERM_CODE
    AND so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY = iap.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
  LEFT JOIN iap_subject_category AS cat
    ON iap.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = cat.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
  WHERE
    -- restrict to rows that are clearly IAP offerings: subject_offered or related course_catalog tables sometimes mark IS_OFFERED_IAP.
    -- subject_offered doesn't have IS_OFFERED_IAP in this schema, but course_catalog_subject_offered / cis_course_catalog do.
    -- Check downstream: join on course_catalog_subject_offered to enforce IS_OFFERED_IAP where available.
    so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY IS NOT NULL
    AND so.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
    AND iap.FEE IS NOT NULL
    -- ensure academic year present
    AND so.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL AND so.TERM_CODE <> ''
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(icf.CATEGORY_TITLE, 'UNCLASSIFIED') AS category_name,
  icf.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS academic_year,
  SUM(icf.FEE_CHARGED) AS total_fee_collected,
  COUNT(DISTINCT icf.SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID) AS total_number_of_IAP_subjects,
  MIN(icf.ENROLLMENT) AS min_enrollment,
  MAX(icf.ENROLLMENT) AS max_enrollment
FROM iap_cleaned_numeric_fields AS icf
-- Only include rows that appear to be IAP: ensure they came from iap_subject_detail (fee exists) and/or category exists.
WHERE icf.ACADEMIC_YEAR IS NOT NULL AND icf.ACADEMIC_YEAR <> ''
GROUP BY
  icf.CATEGORY_TITLE,
  icf.ACADEMIC_YEAR
ORDER BY
  icf.ACADEMIC_YEAR DESC,
  category_name ASC

rows.question: For each sponsor of the independent activity periods, list the sponsor name, number of sessions held, the total number of enrollment, the minimum and maximum fee, the number of sessions with info, and the number of sessions without info.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH iap_sessions AS (
  SELECT
    s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS SESSION_ID,
    COALESCE(sd.TERM_CODE, s.SESSION_DATE) AS TERM_INDICATOR,
    s.HAS_SESSION_INFO AS HAS_SESSION_INFO,
    -- ENROLLMENT stored in iap_subject_detail.ENROLLMENT_TYPE per schema; treat as numeric if possible
    -- Some rows may have non-numeric ENROLLMENT_TYPE; attempt cast to signed, NULL if not numeric
    NULLIF(sd.ENROLLMENT_TYPE, '') AS ENROLLMENT_RAW,
    sd.FEE AS FEE,
    sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY AS SPONSOR_ID,
    sp.SPONSOR_NAME AS SPONSOR_NAME
  FROM iap_subject_session s
  LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail sd
    ON s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
  LEFT JOIN iap_subject_sponsor sp
    ON sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = sp.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
  WHERE (
    -- restrict to rows whose term indicator denotes IAP.
    -- TERM_CODE (in detail) or SESSION_DATE (in session) may contain 'IAP'
    COALESCE(sd.TERM_CODE, s.SESSION_DATE) LIKE CONCAT('%', 'IAP', '%')
  )
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(SPONSOR_NAME, 'UNKNOWN') AS SPONSOR_NAME,
  COUNT(*) AS SESSION_COUNT,
  -- sum enrollment: try to convert ENROLLMENT_RAW to signed; non-numeric will be treated as 0 via CAST of NULL -> NULL then COALESCE
  SUM(COALESCE(CAST(ENROLLMENT_RAW AS SIGNED), 0)) AS TOTAL_ENROLLMENT,
  -- MIN and MAX over FEE; FEE is int per schema so MIN/MAX will be numeric or NULL
  MIN(FEE) AS MIN_FEE,
  MAX(FEE) AS MAX_FEE,
  SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_SESSION_INFO = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS SESSIONS_WITH_INFO,
  SUM(CASE WHEN HAS_SESSION_INFO = 'N' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS SESSIONS_WITHOUT_INFO
FROM iap_sessions
GROUP BY COALESCE(SPONSOR_NAME, 'UNKNOWN')
ORDER BY SPONSOR_NAME

rows.question: What are the individual's email and name, academic year, total number of IAP subjects, the minimum and maximum fees, and the total course enrollment for each individual and academic year?
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  edp.EMAIL_ADDRESS AS email,
  edp.FULL_NAME AS name,
  COALESCE(iad.CREATE_DATE, iad.LAST_ACTIVITY_DATE, iss.SESSION_DATE) AS academic_year,
  COUNT(DISTINCT iad.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY, iad.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY, iad.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY, iad.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY) AS total_iap_subjects,
  MIN(iad.FEE) AS min_fee,
  MAX(iad.FEE) AS max_fee,
  SUM(COALESCE(iad.MAX_ENROLLMENT, CAST(iad.ATTENDANCE AS UNSIGNED), 0)) AS total_course_enrollment
FROM drupal_employee_directory edp
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_person isp
  ON (isp.PERSON_EMAIL IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(LOWER(isp.PERSON_EMAIL)) = TRIM(LOWER(edp.EMAIL_ADDRESS)))
     OR (isp.PERSON_NAME IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(LOWER(isp.PERSON_NAME)) = TRIM(LOWER(edp.FULL_NAME)))
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_session iss
  ON isp.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY IS NOT NULL
     AND iss.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = isp.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail iad
  ON iad.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY = isp.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
     OR iad.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = iss.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
WHERE edp.EMAIL_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(edp.EMAIL_ADDRESS) <> ''
  AND (iad.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY IS NOT NULL OR isp.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY IS NOT NULL)
GROUP BY
  edp.MIT_ID,
  edp.EMAIL_ADDRESS,
  edp.FULL_NAME,
  COALESCE(iad.CREATE_DATE, iad.LAST_ACTIVITY_DATE, iss.SESSION_DATE)
ORDER BY
  edp.EMAIL_ADDRESS ASC,
  academic_year DESC

rows.question: What is the term code, term description, total number of IAP sessions, total fee collected, and minimum and maximum enrollment for each term code?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH term_descriptions AS (
  SELECT
    `TERM_CODE`,
    `TERM_DESCRIPTION`
  FROM `academic_terms`
),
-- identify iap sessions: rows in subject_iap_schedule and/or iap_subject_detail that indicate IAP
iap_sessions AS (
  SELECT
    s.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
    s.SESSION_NUMBER,
    sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY,
    sd.FEE,
    sd.MAX_ENROLLMENT
  FROM `subject_iap_schedule` s
  LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_detail` sd
    ON s.TERM_CODE = sd.TERM_CODE
    AND s.IAP_DAY = sd.IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION -- keep join flexible; primary join by TERM_CODE, allow sd fields
  WHERE
    -- consider rows where term indicates IAP in either table: subject_iap_schedule TERM_CODE looks like IAP terms,
    -- or iap_subject_detail.TERM_CODE exists; also include rows where any IAP-indicator columns explicitly equal 'IAP' or 'Y'
    (
      s.TERM_CODE LIKE '%IAP%' -- TERM_CODE naming convention may include 'IAP' (keeps sessions from schedule)
      OR sd.TERM_CODE LIKE '%IAP%'
      OR sd.IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION = 'IAP'
      OR sd.IS_CANCELLED = 'IAP'
      OR sd.ENROLLMENT_TYPE = 'IAP'
      OR sd.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL -- include iap_subject_detail rows joined by TERM_CODE (covers real IAP sessions)
    )
),
-- aggregate per TERM_CODE, excluding NULL fee and NULL enrollment from respective aggregations
iap_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    TERM_CODE,
    COUNT(*) AS TOTAL_IAP_SESSIONS,
    SUM(CASE WHEN FEE IS NOT NULL THEN FEE ELSE 0 END) AS TOTAL_FEE_COLLECTED,
    -- for min/max enrollment, exclude NULLs by using a derived filtered aggregation
    MIN(NULLIF(MAX_ENROLLMENT, NULL)) AS MIN_ENROLLMENT,
    MAX(NULLIF(MAX_ENROLLMENT, NULL)) AS MAX_ENROLLMENT
  FROM iap_sessions
  GROUP BY TERM_CODE
)
SELECT
  ia.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  td.TERM_DESCRIPTION AS TERM_DESCRIPTION,
  ia.TOTAL_IAP_SESSIONS AS TOTAL_IAP_SESSIONS,
  ia.TOTAL_FEE_COLLECTED AS TOTAL_FEE_COLLECTED,
  ia.MIN_ENROLLMENT AS MIN_ENROLLMENT,
  ia.MAX_ENROLLMENT AS MAX_ENROLLMENT
FROM iap_aggregates ia
LEFT JOIN term_descriptions td
  ON ia.TERM_CODE = td.TERM_CODE
ORDER BY ia.TERM_CODE
